narrative.text:
NARRATIVE:

FACTS OF ENCOUNTER/ ARREST:

On July 11th, 2017, United States Border Patrol Agents assigned to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Station received information of a possible visa overstay living in Lake Leelanau, Michigan. Based on that information and record checks that were conducted, agents identified a total of three possible overstays. First subject was identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] COB: India. Second subject was identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] COB: India. Third subject was identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] DOB: [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] COB: India. On August 10, 2017, Border Patrol Agents [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] were [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] and observed [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] working inside the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] in Lake Leelanau, Michigan. At approximately 8:45p.m., both Agents observed [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] leaving that grocery store and walking south on [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Agents approached [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , identified themselves as United States Border Patrol Agents, and questioned him as to his immigration status. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] freely stated that his visa had expired and he was a citizen and national of India who was not in possession of any U.S. Immigration documents that would allow him to live, to work, or to remain in the U.S. legally. While talking to [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] , Agents were approached by a female, later identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] . Agents identified themselves as United States Border Patrol Agents, and questioned her as to her immigration status. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] freely stated that her visa had expired and she was a citizen and national of India who was not in possession of any U.S. Immigration documents that would allow her to live, to work, or to remain in the U.S. legally. Both subjects were arrested and taken into custody for being in the United States illegally. Agents [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] then, accompanied both [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] to their home in Lake Leelenau, Michigan, in order to retrieve [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] needed medications. While there, they encountered a male, later identified as [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] . Agents [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] identified themselves as United States Border Patrol Agents, and questioned him as to his immigration status. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] freely admitted that his visa had expired and he was a citizen and national of India who was not in possession of any U.S. Immigration documents that would allow him to live, to work, or to remain in the U.S. legally. At that time, [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was subsequently arrested and taken into custody. All three subjects were then transported to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station at approximately 2142 hours for further investigation and processing. Once at the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station, [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] fingerprints and photograph were obtained and entered into the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] systems. Additional records checks were conducted through Detroit Sector Radio. The following was discovered:

IMMIGRATION HISTORY:

8/11/2004 Arrived into the United States as a B1 Visitor Visa 10/20/2007 Changed status to an F1 Student. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] 08/21/2008 Changed status to H4 Child of H-1B1 5/4/2009 Application to extend/change Non-Immigrant Status to F1 Student 9/13/2013 Visa Overstay 7/22/2014 Applied for Re-instatement of Status 9/5/2014 Denial of Re-instatement of Status 10/16/2014 Denial notice ordered, Status revoked 11/28/2014 Appealed Revocation Order 1/09/2015 Denied Appeal Issued A# [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)]

INADMISIBILITY/DEPORTABILITY:

237(a)(1)(B) Nonimmigrant Overstay

CRIMINAL HISTORY:

None FBI# [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)]

DISPOSITION:

[REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] received a Warrant of Arrest/Notice to Appear. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] (along with all of his property) will be held at the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] County Jail pending his removal proceedings. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] did not receive a bond due to the new Executive Order Implementing the President's Border Security and Immigration Enforcement Improvements Policies dated February 20, 2017. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] appeared to be lucid and in good health, however has General Anxiety issues and has been prescribed [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] to be taken as needed. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was notified of his right to contact the Indian Consulate Office at 2:00 A.M., to which he declined to exercise (as witnessed by Border Patrol Agents [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] ). [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] was given a list of free legal services and copies of the I-862 and I-826. [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] does not have any fear of returning to his native country of India.
